title: A piece of junk but a great Frizzbee!!
text:
I bought my Aeropress Coffee Maker about a month ago and I love
it. Its a 6 star product. Besides making a great cup of coffee it is extremely easy to use and especially to clean after you use it. I use the " inverted " method to make coffee and follow the instructions on You Tube closely.
I've been using paper filters without a problem but the You Tube Video suggests an even better cup of coffee by using a stainless reusable filter, hence this piece of junk.
First of all it doesn't fit at all easily. Its too thick. I followed the instructions that came with it and tried loosening up the filter holder by using several layers of paper filters. After some really tough twisting and finger hurting, I got the thing on the Aeropress, just barely and made a cup of coffee. I thought that things would continue to get better the more u used the filter but they didn,'t. After fighting with this thing for several cups I burned my fingers trying to get it on.
The second and not nearly as important problem is that it made the Aero Press more difficult to clean. When u remove the filter holder the coffee spills all over instead of staying in the press so you can just place it over the drain and push on the plunger
They send a brief instruction page with the filter and suggest that if all else fails you can call them and they'll give you some further tips on securing the filter to the Aero Press. I don't have time to fool around with them. If they have something to add why not just incule it with the instructions. Paper is cheap, time isn't
I do want you to know that the filter does make a great frizzbee. Made it over my neighbors house on the first try.
I don't know if the other brands of filters are better but this is a definite "don't buy"

title: I hate this ice maker.
text:
The good, the bad, the ugly!

We are replacing yet another ice maker. This OEM is leaking in two spots in the tray, causing two months of &350+ water bills! This is our third ice maker in 11yrs. When the OEM gives it a one year warranty, that kinda tells you they aren’t made to last the life of the fridge.

First the good.
It came with a wiring harness, which I was not expecting. The bottom of covered so there aren’t any accidental shocks to the back of the hand when reaching in for ice, it happened to me once. The two top mounts have large slots that allow the screws to be pre-screwed and the unit is simply “hung” on the screws. The OEM Whirlpool has holes that were always a pain to hold the unit, nut driver, and screw while trying to line it up. It has two sets of fingers to sweep the ice. Finally, it arrived next day!

The bad:
The wiring harness plug is not the correct plug for my Maytag fridge. Not a problem, it’s very easy to swap the OEM plug. The cubes are HALF the size of OEM! The tray that the fill tube pours water into is a little too low and water is splashing out as it fills. Which means the last two trays aren’t filling completely.

The ugly:
We have had it for 3 days and it still hasn’t filled the OEM bin halfway. The motor is so weak, it can’t get out of its own way! The fingers often get stuck and need to be manually moved to dislodge it from being stuck. Sometimes lifting the bale to off/on a few times has triggered it. There have been SEVERAL times that “jumping” it. Even then, it has been so weak that it screams in agony. I have been wrestling with the water fill level dial on the side because the factory setting was creating a big block of 8 pieces of ice.

Final thoughts:
Maybe so have a lemon? Perhaps the seller will see this review and reach out to me and die whatever it takes to help our lives get back to normal. If not, this ice maker is going back. I knew there was a slight risk buying aftermarket parts. I have never had any problems buying parts for our Whirlpool washer & dryer. This ice maker cost me $65. Maytag has the OEM unit for $140 shipped. My local Whirlpool parts distributor has the same OEM that is now being replaced for the third time in 11yrs for $220.

I guess the thing that REALLY PISSES ME OFF is that the ice cubes are HALF the size (length) of OEM and it takes an hour to make a batch of ice. The OEM makes ice in 20 minutes, like clockwork.

title: I love this stove--when it works.......
text:
I purchased this GE profile induction stove early in 2016 From Sears appliances. It worked great for the first 18 months or so. Induction cooking is great--heat controlled, easy to clean, fast--I don't think I could go back to gas (using the smoke detector for a cooking timer) or regular electric (waiting for the unit to finally heat up, then cleaning all the unit pans from the boil-overs and grease splatters that inevitably happen). BUT, after the first 18 months, this stove has been on about a 3-day work week--it cannot be depended upon to work on any given day or time. It intermittently shuts itself off and refuses to work, then a day or two later will magically agree to come to work for no apparent reason whatsoever. Just try to invite friends to dinner and the stove will go on vacation. Christmas dinner was an adventure.

The circuit breaker for the stove has become my best friend. Sometimes, I can turn off the breaker for a minute or two, and the stove will work. Sometimes I get error code FA92. Thank goodness I purchased an extended warranty, because the repair folks have replaced the big "motherboard" that makes the whole thing work twice, replaced the fan once, and the components for the big stove top unit is coming in a couple weeks. There was another repair for the panel under the touch panel. I'm sure the cost of these repairs (under my extended warranty) cost more than the stove in the first place, so if you buy one of these, be sure to get the warranty!

So in a nutshell, I really like induction cooking. Its clean, safe, and controllable. The downside is that it is a giant computer and if one thing shuts down, the whole stove is dead (except sometimes the oven will work---sometimes) Repair people can only replace components, not really track down problems other than looking up the error code and hope they guessed right.

I am hoping that my stove is just a lemon, and that other stoves, even of the same model, work flawlessly for years, because my next stove (and I don't think this one will ever get fixed) will also be an induction stove.

title: Not worth it. Get a Bialetti stove top instead.
text:
It is solid steel and fits ok (hard at first but then one can learn how to load it without jamming it into the machine - Pixie)
The not so good news is that I have not found a way to get a strong enough coffee, comparable to the nespresso cups. I am not talking about the cream, which is less and not as dense, I am talking about the flavor. I tested different quantities of coffee (espresso ground) and the best was well below acceptable. The other issue is that no matter the amount of coffee in the capsule, a significant amount of water was lost in the process and went down in the tray. We all know that the capsules are smaller than the original disposable nespresso to fit them in the machine without damaging the loading mechanism, but I was not expecting the waste of water and such a poor flavor.

Washing was ok. Loading them a bit of a pain (especially early in the morning, right out of bed, if I forgot to get them ready the night before)

I have no experience with other brands of reusable capsules, but I suspect they all have similar challenges based on my research prior to buying these. I bought them because the price was ok enough to give it a try but they ended up in my kitchen drawer after a week of use.

I wish someone could come out with a better product. Frankly, for the price, I get a much better result with my old and lifelong trusted Bialetti stove top Coffees maker. Not much cream, but a good and reliable espresso.
